claim_001.label: SUPPORTED
claim_001.text: When a first parameter type is available, optional() assigns t | None to the val annotation of the generated converter.

evidence.note: The frozen diff replaces typing.Optional[t] with t | None for optional_converter.__annotations__['val'].

claim_001.rationale: The annotation assignment is directly observable in the frozen production diff.

claim_002.label: SUPPORTED
claim_002.text: When a return type is available, optional() assigns rt | None to the return annotation of the generated converter.

evidence.note: The frozen diff replaces typing.Optional[rt] with rt | None for optional_converter.__annotations__['return'].

claim_002.rationale: The return annotation assignment is directly observable in the frozen production diff.

claim_003.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_003.text: The change modifies how optional() handles None values at runtime.
claim_003.rationale: The frozen diff changes type annotation syntax only. The None branches and wrapped converter calls are unchanged.

claim_004.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_004.text: The change was introduced primarily to improve runtime performance.
claim_004.rationale: The frozen diff and commit title concern dropping Python 3.9 and modernizing type annotation syntax; they do not establish runtime performance as the primary motive.
